narration: The analyst asks what drove Company A's revenue growth and whether that growth is sustainable. The financial table compares the prior and current quarter: revenue rises from RMB100 million to RMB110 million, while sales volume rises from 1.0 million to 1.1 million units. Meeting notes identify restocking as a shipment driver. One research report considers demand recovery sufficient to sustain growth, while the other considers continued restocking uncertain. The analyst must find relevant sources, extract data and calculate changes, compare these views and record the reasoning. Repeated searching, extraction and checking take time away from assessing the business. This page describes the existing human workflow, before introducing an LLM proposal.

narration: Tianhong's reported approach separates structuring the analysis from obtaining data and making the investment judgment. The LLM organizes a change in net profit into revenue, cost of sales and expenses, then links those categories to operating drivers. Revenue depends on sales volume and selling price; materials and production costs affect cost of sales; distribution and selling costs affect expenses. Data feeds and calculation tools supply the evidence and numerical work. The decomposition connects each earnings category to its operating evidence. Analysts use the driver analysis to assess the quality and sustainability of earnings growth.
